answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the ledge check immediately, the beacon audit keeps the resolved set and the lantern replay publishes exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 99 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 99 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
